title: Implement useInterval (Dan Abramov Pattern)
concept: Mutable Saved Callback Ref to Eliminate Interval Teardowns
problemStatement: Implement `createUseIntervalManager()` that accepts an interval callback and delay. Whenever the callback changes, update the internal saved reference WITHOUT restarting the interval timer.
interviewTrap: Setting `callback` in the `useEffect` dependency array restarts the interval on every render, resetting the timer tick.

testCases.name: Invokes the freshest callback without restarting the timer
testCases.testFn: const manager = createUseIntervalManager(); let calledWith = ''; manager.setCallback(() => { calledWith = 'old'; }); manager.start(20); manager.setCallback(() => { calledWith = 'fresh-callback'; }); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 35)); manager.stop(); return calledWith;

testCases.name: stop() halts timer ticks cleanly
testCases.testFn: const manager = createUseIntervalManager(); let count = 0; manager.setCallback(() => count++); manager.start(15); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 25)); manager.stop(); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 30)); return count;

testCases.name: Does not start timer if delay is null
testCases.testFn: const manager = createUseIntervalManager(); let count = 0; manager.setCallback(() => count++); manager.start(null); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 30)); return count;

details.name: Invokes the freshest callback without restarting the timer
Does not start timer if delay is null

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Standard `setInterval` does not play well with React because it captures closures from when the interval was established. Dan Abramov's canonical `useInterval` pattern solves this using a mutable ref (`savedCallback`) that is updated on every render, allowing the interval to invoke the freshest callback without resetting the timer.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Create a mutable reference: `const savedCallback = useRef()`.
In `useEffect`, update the ref on every render: `savedCallback.current = callback`.
In a secondary `useEffect` dependent only on `[delay]`:
Setup timer: `const id = setInterval(() => savedCallback.current(), delay)`.
Provide a `stop()` method to set delay to null or clear the interval.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: `useRef` returns a stable object `{ current: value }` whose reference identity never changes across renders. Mutating `ref.current` updates the value in-place without triggering re-renders and without changing the dependency array of the interval effect. The interval closure calls `savedCallback.current()`, reading the fresh function reference dynamically.
edgeCasesHandled: Dynamic callbacks with closed-over state always execute with latest state.
Changing `delay` dynamically adjusts interval timing cleanly.
Passing `delay: null` pauses the interval without unmounting.

specifications: Dan Abramov: Making setInterval Declarative with React Hooks (Overreacted.io)
React Official Docs: Referencing Values with Refs
verifiedRules: Refs provide a mutable escape hatch across renders without re-triggering effects.
Separating callback storage from timer lifecycle prevents timer reset thrashing.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does Dan Abramov's useInterval pattern eliminate interval reset thrashing?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: A standard `useEffect` tied to `[delay, callback]` resets the browser timer every time `callback` changes (e.g. on every render). The `useInterval` pattern uses a mutable ref: `const savedCallback = useRef(callback)`. Inside `useEffect`, it updates `savedCallback.current = callback` on every render. A separate effect sets up the timer ONCE (`setInterval(() => savedCallback.current(), delay)`). The interval never resets, yet always executes the freshest callback.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The canonical custom hook design pattern question.

realWorldUseCases.description: Polling server metrics every 1000ms while accessing live React state without resetting the clock on every state update.

howToExplain.opening: The useInterval pattern decouples timer lifecycle from callback state by routing execution through a mutable ref that updates on every render.
keyPoints: Mutable ref holds the latest callback reference.
Updating ref.current does not trigger re-renders or reset effects.
Timer effect depends only on delay, keeping the timer stable.
Passing delay: null pauses the interval cleanly.
howToExplain.closingImpression: This pattern is the foundational model for bridging imperative browser APIs with declarative React lifecycles.
analogies: A secretary relaying instructions: the boss updates instructions on the memo board daily, but the delivery truck runs on a fixed weekly schedule without changing routes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding callback to the interval effect dependency array.
commonMistakes.why: Causes the interval to clear and re-create on every render, ruining steady tick timing.
commonMistakes.correct: Store callback in a ref and keep the effect dependent only on delay.

followUpDeepDive.question: Why does Dan Abramov call refs a 'bail out' mechanism in declarative React?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Refs provide an escape hatch from pure functional declarative immutability, allowing mutable pointers to persist across renders without participating in the reactive dependency graph.
